topic: South Africa player sets new T20 scoring record
headline_marked: 188* in 79 balls: [[Pretorius sets new T20 scoring record]]
headline: 188* in 79 balls: Pretorius sets new T20 scoring record
summary: South Africa's Lhuan-dre Pretorius smashed the highest individual score in the 20-over format, surpassing Chris Gayle's long-standing record.
details: Lhuan-dre Pretorius scored an unbeaten 188 runs from just 79 balls for South Africa's Titans franchise against the Knights in a domestic CSA T20 Challenge fixture on Friday.
The 20-year-old left-hander launched 13 sixes and 15 fours during his explosive innings, setting a new world record for the highest individual score in the 20-over format.
Pretorius surpassed the previous record of 175 not out, which was set by West Indies legend Chris Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors in the IPL in 2013.
The Titans finished their innings on 267 for three, with Pretorius narrowly missing a double-century as he ran out of overs.
Despite being blighted by injury recently, the young batter has been in stellar form, having previously scored 101 off 53 balls for South Africa against Namibia last month.
caption:
188 runs, 79 balls, and a world record! Lhuan-dre Pretorius just rewrote the T20 history books.

Lhuan-dre Pretorius scored an unbeaten 188 runs from just 79 balls for South Africa's Titans franchise against the Knights in a domestic CSA T20 Challenge fixture on Friday.

The 20-year-old left-hander launched 13 sixes and 15 fours during his explosive innings, setting a new world record for the highest individual score in the 20-over format.

Pretorius surpassed the previous record of 175 not out, which was set by West Indies legend Chris Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors in the IPL in 2013.

The Titans finished their innings on 267 for three, with Pretorius narrowly missing a double-century as he ran out of overs.

Despite being blighted by injury recently, the young batter has been in stellar form, having previously scored 101 off 53 balls for South Africa against Namibia last month.
